reading.body:
Lenovo's US arm filed 10 AI lobbying reports, naming 15 separate bills, which shows a hardware maker treating AI regulation as a broad legislative problem rather than a single-issue concern.

The filings name 15 bills across both chambers, from HR 321 to S 3952, and eight lobbyists work the account. Jon Beamer appears on all 10 filings and Heather Smith on 9, so the account is carried by a small core rather than spread thin. The bill count is the notable figure: a company filing on 15 distinct pieces of AI legislation is tracking the issue across many fronts at once.

For AI specifically, this is the policy layer beneath the compute buildout. Lenovo sells the servers and devices that AI workloads run on, so rules touching AI deployment, procurement, and hardware supply chains land on its business directly. The breadth of bills suggests the company is not waiting for one comprehensive AI statute but engaging the pieces as they move.

What the data does not say is what Lenovo argued. A firm that files for a client reports that it lobbied on an issue, not the position it took, so nothing here indicates whether the company supported or opposed any bill. The filings also do not show spending amounts, committee activity, or outcomes, and they cover only this one client's reports as held by this site.

summary: LENOVO (UNITED STATES) INC. filed 10 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 401108077.
